input.quote: 11.1 For Convenience. Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least one (1) years' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount equal to REDACTED of the Estimated Remaining Value.
input.rationale: The Term runs eight years (p0049), and the only Customer convenience exit (11.1) requires a full year's written notice — far outside the 60–90 day fallback — plus an early-termination fee measured as a percentage of the Estimated Remaining Value, i.e. the Monthly Base Fee (or higher three-month average) multiplied by every month left in an up-to-eight-year term (p0039). That is orders of magnitude above the fallback cap of three months' fees, is stacked with unamortized Conversion costs and disposition Expenses, and is expressly carved out of the Section 13.4 liability limitation. Both material terms (notice and fee) fail the fallback, so this is a deviation. Our redline sits at the fallback rather than the preferred 30-day/no-fee position because the up-front conversion investment in this outsourcing makes preferred disproportionate; we have kept M&I's unamortized Conversion costs recoverable. Noted but not separately flagged: Section 10.2 (p0180) lets M&I withdraw non-Core Services at any time on 90 days' notice, which is at the edge of (not below) the 90-day walk-away threshold and is mitigated by the good-faith Base Fee reduction in p0181.

proposal.summary: Cut convenience notice from one year to 90 days and cap the termination fee at three months' Monthly Base Fee, with a refund of prepaid Fees.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] A one-year notice period plus an uncapped percentage of the Estimated Remaining Value (carved out of the liability cap) is a penalty rather than a convenience exit, so we have moved to 90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' Monthly Base Fee and a refund of prepaid Fees. We have left M&I's unamortized Conversion costs recoverable as a fair compromise to our preferred position of 30 days' notice with no fee.

ops.oldText: 11.1 For Convenience. Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least one (1) years' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount equal to REDACTED of the Estimated Remaining Value. The Termination for Convenience Fee shall apply to any early termination of this Agreement other than pursuant to an Event of Default on the part of Customer or M&I or pursuant to Section 11.3 below. Fifty percent of the Termination for Convenience Fee shall be paid to M&I within thirty (30) days following the date of Customer's notice and the remaining 50% shall be paid to M&I within thirty (30) days prior to the Effective Date of Termination. In addition to the foregoing, Customer shall pay to M&I, any unamortized Conversion or other costs, reasonable Expenses in connection with the disposition of equipment, facilities and contracts related to M&I's performance of the Services on behalf of Customer. The Termination for Convenience Fee shall not be subject to the limitations set forth in Section 13.4.
ops.newText: 11.1 For Convenience. Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least ninety (90) days' written notice to M&I, provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount not to exceed three (3) times the Monthly Base Fee in effect as of the Effective Date of Termination. The Termination for Convenience Fee shall apply to any early termination of this Agreement other than pursuant to an Event of Default on the part of Customer or M&I or pursuant to Section 11.3 below. The Termination for Convenience Fee shall be paid to M&I within thirty (30) days following the Effective Date of Termination. In addition to the foregoing, Customer shall pay to M&I any unamortized Conversion costs, and M&I shall refund to Customer any prepaid Fees attributable to the period after the Effective Date of Termination.
